questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: language, culture, academic level, distance, weather

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: not that easy, i didn't have my schedule the before i had to start..

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: i got a student assigend to me who could anwer me a few questions which was nice. He was not from my derpartment though..

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: very hard, I found it very late through a good but very expensive website called spotahome.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Depends how far off campus. Milano is a really big city so you can spend a lot of time on transport. I got a bike so I could bike but biking is not the same as in Copnehagen :)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: hard to figure out on your own.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The only thing I had to do was picking up my student card at a buro. 
About the classes I had to find informtions (where and when, very confusing in the beginning) about the courses online and then you have 2-3 weeks until you have to register for the specific courses online. 
A lot of the classes in my derpartment were overlapping which was a little stressful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Our coordinator was very busy in the beginning of our stay and very hard to get in contact with. After a little time (when we already had figured everything out on our own) he got back to us and was very helpful and nice - just a little too late with his help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The classes i looked up previous to my arrival were almost all overlapping. The times for the classes were very late availabale. So the few days before the semester startet I had to make a complete new schedule. I got into all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to someone who has already been at University of Milan and can explain the basics of how things work around there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was only able to take Master-courses, since these were the only classes in english (in my case). Therefore the classes were way more specific than what I am used (which was nice!) but the level was kind of the same

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was surpised about the classes only beeing lectures and no assignments or homework and missed that actually a little bit..

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Environmental Geochemistry, Biochemistry, Georesources and Sustainability, Statistics and dataanalysis and Economic Botany and Zoology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I especially enjoyed Economic Botany and Zoology and Geochemistry. A big part were the very motivated professors and I think the topics were very interesting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The ESN network made a lot of nice opportunities happen: food tours, beachvolleball, a trip to rom etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take your time to explore Italy!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All the nearby cities! E.g.: Lake Como, lake Maggiore, Lake Garda, Cinque Terre, Bologna, Venice, Verona, Sicilia, Florence...

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
easy: you quickly get used to eat pizza/pasta everyday...
Sometimes it was a little struggle because not all Italians spoke english...

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Stay with other students, meet them at university

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: language

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: spontanity

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look at housing in good time (maybe choose studentsdorm), don't get so scared about university registrations etc., everything works slower but mostly works out in the end and say yes to all opportunies for meeting people or visiting new places.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: learning to get comfortable in a completly new city on your own

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: missing green spaces when living in such a big city

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
